calls.reason: The burst condition isn't met. Reuters describes a crash in China and only a 6% Nasdaq dip in the US, and the IMF treats a wider correction as a risk. Nothing on buyer insolvencies exists yet.

The total can be rebuilt from Crunchbase's $18.2B, a $2.5B revolving credit line and 30% of Amazon's capex. But the credit line may not have been drawn, the 2025 figure is a plan, and the 30% share is his own assumption.

The Nature study and the impossibility paper show persistent errors. The Kalai et al. paper instead blames training and evaluation incentives, so whether the architecture itself is the cause stays contested.

Semafor and ITPro pieces show continuing coverage of rising token bills, but they are spread over months. ITPro also notes token prices fell recently. None of this shows a sudden media-wide realisation.
The GSA releases show discounted access and growing integration. They don't show heavy OpenAI customisation spending or any government service depending on ChatGPT, and the forecast has no deadline.
The vendor launch pages show overlapping assistant functions, plus distinctive features such as Grok's X search. No independent comparison shows the products are, or are not, practical substitutes.
